**SECTION B (Databases)**

The database system of a company has a table PC for details of its personal computers, and a table Employee for details of its employees, with attribute names of obvious meanings. No attribute entry in table PC is unique. However, in table Employee, the entries of EmpNo (for employee number) and UserID are unique to each employee. Table Employee also contains details that indicate the type of personal computer(s) each employee uses. Sample entries for the tables are the following

**Table: PC**

| PC type | Processor | RAM (GB) | Disk Size (TB) |
|---|---|---|---|
| HP | Core i5 | 8 | 1 |
| HP | Core i7 | 16 | 4 |
| Lenovo | Dual Core | 8 | 1 |

**Table: Employee**

| First Name | Last Name | UserID | EmpNo | PC type | Processor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Joe | Bloggs | jbloggs | 25 | HP | Core i7 |
| Mary | Smith | msmith | 80 | Lenovo | Dual Core |

questions.enonce_markdown:
**TASK 3** *(12 Marks)*

a) In your answer booklet, write down the SQL data types you will use to implement your tables described above. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The type of a column is chosen from the kind of value it stores. (In the SQL below the spaces of the printed attribute names are removed: `First Name` becomes `FirstName`, `PC type` becomes `PCType`, `Disk Size (TB)` becomes `DiskSize_TB`.)

**Table PC**

| Attribute | Example | SQL data type | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| PCType | HP, Lenovo | `VARCHAR(30)` | short text of variable length |
| Processor | Core i5, Dual Core | `VARCHAR(30)` | text (it contains letters, digits and spaces) |
| RAM (GB) | 8, 16 | `INTEGER` | a whole number of gigabytes, used in comparisons (RAM > 8) |
| Disk Size (TB) | 1, 4 | `DECIMAL(4,1)` | a number which may have a fractional part (0.5 TB); `INTEGER` is enough for the sample |

**Table Employee**

| Attribute | Example | SQL data type | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| FirstName | Joe | `VARCHAR(30)` | text |
| LastName | Bloggs | `VARCHAR(30)` | text |
| UserID | jbloggs | `VARCHAR(20)` | text (letters), unique for each employee |
| EmpNo | 25, 80 | `INTEGER` | an employee number: a whole number, unique for each employee |
| PCType | HP | `VARCHAR(30)` | text, same type as PC.PCType |
| Processor | Core i7 | `VARCHAR(30)` | text, same type as PC.Processor |

Remarks: columns that describe the same thing in the two tables (PCType, Processor) have the **same type and length**, so that they can be compared in a query. EmpNo is only an identifier, never used in a calculation, so a text type (`VARCHAR`) would also be acceptable; a whole number is the natural choice for a number of employee.

**Marking (5 marks, 0.5 mark per attribute):** a suitable type for each of the ten attributes (text for names, UserID, PCType and Processor; whole number for RAM and EmpNo; a numeric type for the disk size).

questions.enonce_markdown: b) Using your favourite database management system (DBMS), create the tables indicated above. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The tables are created with the DDL (Data Definition Language) of SQL, in any DBMS (MySQL, SQLite, Microsoft Access in SQL view...). Table PC has **no key**, because no attribute of PC is unique (the statement of the section says so); table Employee has `EmpNo` as primary key, and `UserID`, which is also unique, is declared `UNIQUE`.

```sql
CREATE TABLE PC (
    PCType       VARCHAR(30)  NOT NULL,
    Processor    VARCHAR(30)  NOT NULL,
    RAM_GB       INTEGER      NOT NULL,
    DiskSize_TB  DECIMAL(4,1) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Employee (
    FirstName  VARCHAR(30)  NOT NULL,
    LastName   VARCHAR(30)  NOT NULL,
    UserID     VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    EmpNo      INTEGER      PRIMARY KEY,
    PCType     VARCHAR(30),
    Processor  VARCHAR(30)
);
```

**Check by execution** (sqlite3 module of Python): both tables were created without error. Inserting an employee with an existing `UserID` was refused (`UNIQUE constraint failed: Employee.UserID`), and so was an existing `EmpNo` (`UNIQUE constraint failed: Employee.EmpNo`). The names and types of the columns are those of 3(a); the spaces of the printed attribute names are not allowed in plain SQL identifiers (they would have to be quoted).

**Marking (4 marks):** CREATE TABLE PC with its four columns (1 mark); CREATE TABLE Employee with its six columns (1 mark); data types consistent with 3(a) (1 mark); the unique attributes EmpNo and UserID declared (PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE) (1 mark).

The text file is then printed.
